classification.difficultyReason: Derive Pythagoras’ Theorem symbolically from a tangent–secant product.

content.prompt: Show that the Power of a Point Theorem implies the Pythagorean Theorem using the diagram below.

spec.description: Unfilled circle with centre O, tangent a, vertical radius b and sloping centre-directed segment split into c−b and b. No additional point names or angle marks are printed.
spec.mathematics: The tangent and radius form perpendicular sides a and b. The centre-directed segment is the hypotenuse c.

answer.short:
$c^2=a^2+b^2$.

Extend the sloping segment across the circle and use $a^2=(c-b)(c+b)$.
answer.worked:
The radius is $b$, so the sloping segment to $O$ has length $c$. Extend it through $O$ to the far side of the circle; the whole secant has length $c+b$. By the Power of a Point Theorem,
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=(c-b)(c+b)\\a^2&=c^2-b^2\\a^2+b^2&=c^2.\end{align*}$$
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so this establishes Pythagoras’ Theorem.
